data.one_liner: Flutter widget for real-time audio visualizations using custom painter or shaders.
data.what_it_does: AudioFlux captures audio from playback or microphone and renders it as waveforms, FFT spectra, or GPU‑accelerated shader effects. It provides a configurable widget that updates automatically as audio data changes.
use_when: You need a real‑time visual representation of audio in a Flutter app
You want to display waveforms, frequency spectra, or custom shader effects
You are already using flutter_soloud or flutter_recorder for audio
avoid_when: You only need audio playback without visualization
You lack the ability to add platform permissions or shader assets
You require a pure Dart solution without native dependencies
strengths: Supports both CustomPainter and shader‑based rendering
Works on all major Flutter platforms
Integrates with flutter_soloud and flutter_recorder for live audio capture
weaknesses: Relies on external packages that may introduce breaking changes
data.setup_notes: Add flutter_soloud and flutter_recorder to pubspec, configure microphone/audio permissions, register shader assets in flutter: shaders section, then use AudioFlux widget

alternatives.name: just_audio
alternatives.why_pick_it: Provides robust audio playback without the extra visualization layer

data.minimal_example:
AudioFlux(
  fluxType: FluxType.waveform,
  dataSource: DataSources.soloud,
  modelParams: ModelParams(
    waveformParams: WaveformPainterParams(barsWidth: 2, barSpacingScale: 0.5, chunkSize: 1),
  ),
)
